Subject: End-of-Q scoring: handback, evidence bundle, and identified blindspots

Team —

Attached is the handback for Q2 endpoint; I zipped the evidence bundle and included the raw scoring CSV. Two quick framing notes before you review:

- What you have: qtr2_scores_handback.csv contains final suggested numerical adjustments from the scoring panel and the linked evidence in qtr2_evidence_package.zip.
- Asks: (1) Confirm any final changes by EOD Monday (4/19) so I can bake into the narrative; (2) Flag any ‘blindspots’ you want called out in the exec summary (we should be explicit if a metric is known to be noisy or has external dependencies).

Quick items I want leadership guidance on:
1) "Model inference cost per 1M tokens" — panel recommended a -8% adjustment due to late discovery of caching misconfiguration. This materially changes the cost CFR. If we accept the adjustment, we should call it out in the QBR narrative as an operational remediation.
2) "Dedicated renewals influence" — Marissa and I disagreed on whether pipeline motions should count toward the growth objective this quarter; panel split 60/40 in favor of partial credit.

Proposed timeline: final scores consolidated by 4/19 EOD; narrative draft for exec slide deck to be circulated 4/20 AM for review.

Attachments: qtr2_evidence_package.zip (contains sample traces, cost runs, and the scoring forms), qtr2_scores_handback.csv, narrative_draft_v1.docx (skeleton).

Thanks — please reply with short bullets (agree / disagree / escalate) so I can track decisions.

— Soojin

Soojin —

Thx for the packet, read it quickly this morning. Two quick responses:

- Cost metric: I agree with the panel adjustment. The caching bug is an operational regression; we should accept the -8% adjustment and add a clear remediation bullet in the narrative (owner: infra reliability; ETA: mid-May).
- Dedicated renewals: I side with partial credit. We committed to at-risk customers earlier in the quarter and did operational work that materially improved renewal cadence — give 50% credit with a footnote explaining the reasoning.

I attached a one-page comment doc (redlines) with micro edits to the narrative skeleton. If you want, I can pair with Marissa to align the footnote language.

Team —

I skimmed the evidence and Ben's notes. Agree to accept the cost adjustment but we need a single-line attribution in the slide: "Adjusted to reflect post-hoc discovery of caching misconfiguration; remediation in progress." Keep it succinct — execs will not want the full technical detail in the slide.

On the renewals footnote: Marissa, can you consolidate the renewal-related artifacts into a 1-slide appendix (call out the contracts, dates, and commercial outreach) so we can hand that to GTM during the deck review?

Also, two small asks for the narrative voice:
- Use active ownership language ("Infra replaced misconfigured cache; mitigation complete by 5/14") rather than passive.
- Prefer one quantified line for impact (e.g., "estimated $Xk monthly savings after fix"). If we don't have a confidence interval, mark it as provisional.

Laura

Thanks for driving this, Soojin. High-level: accept the panel's cost adjustment and the partial credit on renewals. A couple of framing requests for the exec narrative:

1) Lead with the operational remediation and what it means for our cost guidance this year. Execs want a clear implication line up front.
2) Put a single slide after the score table that lists the three biggest uncertainties (cache config, measurement lag on dedicated renewals, and a small sampling bias in the usage telemetry). Call them out as "known uncertainties" with owners and ETA to close.

Soojin — please prepare a 200–300 word narrative paragraph for the slide deck that we can copy verbatim into the QBR executive summary. Keep tone facts-first, 1-2 remediation bullets, and one forward-looking ask. If you can get to me by 4/20 09:00 PT I will sign off.

Vivek

Folks —

Thanks for the rapid review. Attached are the narrative_draft_v1.docx and a condensed 250-word exec paragraph (pasted below) for copy/paste into the QBR slides. I've also added the slide-appendix items Laura requested to the Drive folder linked above.

--- Exec paragraph (250 words) ---
Q2 scoring reflects progress on product velocity and customer traction, tempered by an operational regression that impacted inference unit economics. The scoring panel adjusted the cost-per-1M-tokens metric to reflect a discovered caching misconfiguration; Infra has implemented a mitigation and is tracking a full remediation with completion expected by 2027-05-14. We are accepting a partial credit allocation for Dedicated renewals given sustained sales outreach and product work that materially improved conversion for a cohort of at-risk accounts.

Key actions: (1) Infra to complete remediation and publish post-fix cost runs (owner: Infra Reliability, ETA: 5/14); (2) GTM to assemble renewal appendix for audit (owner: Sales Ops, ETA: 4/22); (3) Product to monitor early indicators and report back at the mid-May ops review (owner: Product Analytics, ETA: 5/10).

Forward ask: leadership approval to include the accepted score adjustments and footnotes in the QBR deck. If there are objections, call them out in reply and I will reconcile immediately.

--- end paragraph ---

I will merge final numeric adjustments into qtr2_scores_handback.csv and publish a clean copy to the drive once I hear no objections by EOD 4/19.

Thanks — Soojin
